tasks.name: Use dates, JSON, heaps, and bisect

concepts.name: itertools.chain
concepts.description: itertools.chain lazily presents multiple iterables as one continuous iterator without first concatenating them into a new list.

concepts.name: itertools.batched
concepts.description: itertools.batched(iterable, n) lazily groups input items into tuples of up to n elements.

concepts.name: itertools.pairwise
concepts.description: itertools.pairwise(iterable) yields overlapping adjacent pairs such as (x0, x1), (x1, x2), and so on.

concepts.name: itertools.starmap
concepts.description: itertools.starmap(func, iterable_of_args) calls func(*args) for each tuple-like argument group from the iterable.

concepts.name: pathlib path composition
concepts.description: pathlib.Path overloads / for path joining and provides object-oriented methods for reading, writing, globbing, and path transformations.

concepts.name: subprocess.run
concepts.description: subprocess.run() is the recommended high-level API for executing a child process and waiting for it to finish.

concepts.name: Timezone-aware datetimes
concepts.description: datetime.now(timezone.utc) creates an aware UTC datetime whose tzinfo is explicit.

concepts.name: json.dumps default hook
concepts.description: json.dumps(..., default=callable) invokes the callable for otherwise non-serializable objects so application-specific conversion can be defined.

concepts.name: heapq.nlargest
concepts.description: heapq.nlargest(n, iterable, key=...) returns the n largest items without sorting the entire input when n is relatively small.

concepts.name: bisect.insort
concepts.description: bisect.insort keeps a list sorted by locating an insertion point with binary search and then inserting the value.

questions.prompt: Apply pow(base, exponent) to each argument pair lazily.
questions.explanation: itertools.starmap(func, iterable_of_args) calls func(*args) for each tuple-like argument group from the iterable. starmap(pow, [(2, 5), (3, 2)]) applies pow to each argument tuple lazily. questions.prompt: Run the command, raise on failure, and capture decoded output.
questions.explanation: subprocess.run() is the recommended high-level API for executing a child process and waiting for it to finish. subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True) raises on a non-zero exit and returns decoded stdout/stderr. Prefer an argument list over shell=True for ordinary commands; shell parsing adds quoting complexity and can create injection risk with untrusted input.

questions.explanation: heapq.nlargest(n, iterable, key=...) returns the n largest items without sorting the entire input when n is relatively small. top = nlargest(10, users, key=lambda u: u.score) directly returns the ten highest-scoring users. content.template:

scores = [10, 20, 40]
{{answer}}
assert scores == [10, 20, 30, 40]

questions.explanation: bisect.insort keeps a list sorted by locating an insertion point with binary search and then inserting the value. insort(scores, new_score) is convenient when maintaining a small sorted list incrementally. Finding the index is logarithmic, but list insertion is still O(n) because later elements must be shifted.
